title: Characteristic ideal of the fine Selmer group and results on $Œº$-invariance under isogeny in the function field case

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Theorem 1.6 in the introduction assumes "H²_fl(K_∞, E_i[p^∞]) = 0, for i = 1, 2", while the restatement as Theorem 5.1 in Section 5 assumes "H^1_fl(K_∞, E_i[p^∞]) = 0, for i = 1, 2". The proof of Theorem 5.1 explicitly uses the vanishing of H²_fl (e.g. "The assumption H²_fl(K_∞, E₁[p^∞]) = 0 implies ..."), so the hypothesis in Section 5 is stated incorrectly.

The hypothesis "G = Gal(K_∞/K) is pro-p" is impossible in the stated setting: K_∞ = K(E[ℓ^∞]) with ℓ ≠ p, and G is an open subgroup of GL₂(Z_ℓ) (stated in §2.8). An open subgroup of GL₂(Z_ℓ) contains copies of Z_ℓ and hence cannot be pro-p for p ≠ ℓ. The hypothesis should be 'pro-ℓ'; as written the theorem is vacuous/contradictory.

The lemma states "|H^1(G, B)| ≤ |B|^d and |H^1(G, B)| ≤ |B|^{d(d-1)/2}" — the same cohomology group is bounded twice by two different quantities. The second bound must be for H^2(G,B) (as in [BL09a, Lemma 4.1]); as printed the statement is self-contradictory (for d=1 it would force |H^1| = 1).

The proof asserts "0 = (A(L_n)⊗Q_p/Z_p)_div" and concludes "lim_n ((A(L_∞)⊗Q_p/Z_p)^{Γ_n})_div = 0". Both are false: A(L_n) is finitely generated (Theorem 2.10), so A(L_n)⊗Q_p/Z_p ≅ (Q_p/Z_p)^{rank} is already divisible and nonzero whenever rank>0; and the direct limit of the divisible parts is A(L_∞)⊗Q_p/Z_p, which is divisible and nonzero whenever A(L_∞) is infinite. Moreover, under Pontryagin duality the p-torsion of X/ω_nX corresponds to the quotient of (A(L_∞)⊗Q_p/Z_p)^{Γ_n} by its maximal divisible subgroup, not to the divisible subgroup itself, so the duality step producing 𝒢 = 0 is invalid as written.

predicted_errors.error_location: Proof of Theorem 5.1, local term argument ('As K_∞ is unramified at every prime v ...')
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The displayed claim "Gal(K_{∞,w}/K_{∞,w}) ≅ ∏_{ℓ≠p} Z_ℓ" is meaningless (the group of a field over itself is trivial), and even in the intended form (absolute Galois/residue-field Galois group being prime-to-p) the argument cannot justify "ker f_4 = coker f_4 = 0": in the ℓ = p case the local terms are p-primary flat cohomology groups of a finite flat p-group scheme A (e.g. H^1_fl(K_w, μ_p) = K_w^*/K_w^{*p}), which are not controlled by the prime-to-p part of the Galois group. The argument is simply imported from the ℓ ≠ p setting where it is valid.

Case 1 is about 𝒦 = K_cyc but the displayed Euler-characteristic formula (14) is written with H^i(G_S(K_∞), A) and E_i[ℓ^∞](K_∞); the sentence "As E₁[ℓ^∞](K_∞) and E₂[ℓ^∞](K_∞) and A are all finite" is false for the trivialising extension K_∞ = K(E[ℓ^∞]), where E[ℓ^∞](K_∞) = E[ℓ^∞] ≅ (Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ)² is infinite. Case 2 then invokes "calculations similar to Case 1" and the same finiteness, which does not hold there.

predicted_errors.error_location: Appendix A (throughout the proof of Theorem A.1)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The appendix treats the ℓ ≠ p case, but the Euler-characteristic/μ-invariant computations are stated with respect to p: "annihilated by a power of p", "μ(M) = ord_p(χ(Γ, M[p^∞]^∨))", "it suffices to calculate the logarithm to the p-base". In the ℓ ≠ p setting these must be ℓ-adic (ord_ℓ, M[ℓ^∞]); as written the computation computes the wrong invariant. The proof also mixes the labels f_i and g_i for the same maps and refers to a nonexistent "equation (A)".

predicted_errors.error_location: Equation (11) in the proof of Theorem 5.1 (and the analogous display (14) in Appendix A)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: From the long exact sequence of 0 → A → E₁[p^∞] → E₂[p^∞] → 0 one gets χ(coker f₂)/χ(ker f₂) = χ(H²(A))·χ(E₂[p^∞](K_∞))·χ(H⁰(A)) / (χ(H¹(A))·χ(E₁[p^∞](K_∞))). The paper writes χ(E₁[p^∞](K_∞)) in the numerator and χ(E₂[p^∞]) in the denominator, i.e. the roles of E₁ and E₂ are interchanged. (The final conclusion is unaffected only because both factors equal 1.)

The deduction is logically invalid: from μ = 0 one gets e_n = λn + O(1) for |Ж^S(A/K_n)| = p^{e_n}; knowing only that |Ш(A/K_n)[p^∞]| grows like p^{μ₁p^n + c} with μ₁ possibly positive gives the bound λn + O(1) ≤ μ₁p^n + c, which does not force λ = 0. The conclusion "we can conclude that λ = 0 and hence the growth of Ж^S(A/K_n) stays bounded" only follows if μ₁ = 0.

For the Frobenius isogeny the kernel is a nontrivial finite flat group scheme of order q (it is non-reduced, with only one rational point). The argument "the order of the kernel of isogeny equals its separable degree, we get that μ(S(E₂/K_∞)^∨) = μ(S(E₁/K_∞)^∨)" confuses the number of points with the order of the group scheme; Theorem 5.1 computes ord_p χ_fl(Spec K, A) with A = ker φ as a finite flat group scheme, and this need not vanish for A = ker(Fr_q).

predicted_errors.error_location: Remark 3.1 together with Theorem 3.2 and the setup of Section 3
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Remark 3.1 asserts unconditionally that "ker(S_n^A) and coker(S_n^A) are both finite and bounded independently of n" by [Tan10, Theorem 4], but the quoted Theorem 3.2 requires "A ... with good ordinary reduction at every place in S", whereas Section 3 defines S to contain the primes of bad reduction of A. The hypotheses of the cited theorem are therefore incompatible with the standing setup (except in the everywhere-unramified case where S can be taken empty).

The proposition contains only item (a), but the proof repeatedly refers to item (b): "To prove (a) and (b)..." and "Now, if we assume that Ж^S(E/L_n) is finite. Then, (b) follows from the fact that coker(f_n) is finite." The statement (b) (presumably finiteness of coker(m_n)) is missing, and Corollary 4.3 relies on it.

The text says "Let us recall the following lemma from [Lee20]:" but no statement of Lemma 2.9 is given (only a garbled pair of displays "0 → A = A[p^∞] → B[p^∞] → C[p^∞] → 0" and "X_div → Y_div → Z_div → W → 0 is exact"). Yet Lemma 2.9 and specifically "Lemma 2.9(iii)" are invoked in the proof of Proposition 3.5, so the key hypotheses of the cited result are unverifiable.

"the characteristic ideals ... are equal, i.e. there is a pseudo-isomorphism R^S(E/K_∞)^∨ ∼ R^S(E/K_∞)^{∨,ι}" — equality of characteristic ideals does not in general imply pseudo-isomorphism of Λ-modules (e.g. Λ/(p²) and Λ/(p)⊕Λ/(p) have the same characteristic ideal but are not pseudo-isomorphic). The stated 'i.e.' is an invalid implication; the conclusion needs the elementary-divisor decomposition, not just the characteristic ideal.

predicted_errors.error_location: Proof of Proposition 4.6 ('Hence, we conclude that (Image f_n)[Φ_n] = 0')
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The conclusion that the image of f_n has no Φ_n-torsion is drawn solely from the fact that E_0(L_{n,v})^• is "isomorphic to countable copies of Q_p" — an isomorphism of Q_p-vector spaces that carries no information about the Γ/Γ_n-action. Since Φ_n-torsion is defined through the Γ-action, the stated argument does not establish (Image f_n)[Φ_n] = 0, which is the key step giving e_m = s_m.

predicted_errors.error_location: Proof of Theorem 5.1 ('which can be easily derived from equation (5)')
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The multiplicativity relation χ(Γ,coker f₁)/χ(Γ,ker f₁) = (χ(Γ,coker f₂)/χ(Γ,ker f₂))×(χ(Γ,ker f₃)/χ(Γ,coker f₃)) follows from the six-term snake-lemma exact sequence displayed just above it, not from equation (5), which is the localization sequence 0 → H^1_fl(U, 𝒜[p^∞]) → H^1_fl(K, A[p^∞]) → ⊕_v ... of Remark 2.3. The internal reference is wrong.

In the ℓ ≠ p part the conjecture is described as "S(E/K_∞)^∨/S(E/K_∞)^∨[p^∞] is a finitely generated Z_ℓ[[H]]-module" — the torsion submodule must be the ℓ-primary one, [ℓ^∞], since the modules are over Z_ℓ[[G]]. Also the M_H(G) statement is attributed to [Pal14, Theorem 4.1] while Proposition 6.2 attributes the same type of result to [Pal14, Theorem 4.4].

The setup says "Let K be a function field in one variable over a finite field F" but immediately specializes "Consider an open dense subset U of C_K = P^1_F", i.e. assumes K = F(t). This contradicts the general setting used later (e.g. Theorem 2.10 with K = F(C) for an arbitrary curve C, and the statements of Theorems 4.9/5.1 for general function fields).

The recursive definition is garbled and mathematically wrong: the Carlitz action is [t](X) = X^q + tX with q = #F, not "t = X^p + tX" (these differ whenever F ≠ F_p), and the lines "1 = X", "t^n = t)" do not define [1](X), [t^n](X). As written the Carlitz module and hence the ramified Z_p-extensions are incorrectly defined.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 1.1 (first application of Theorem 1.1) vs. Remark 1.4
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper advertises as an application that "under the hypothesis that Ж^S(E/K_∞) is finite one can see easily that the μ-invariant of the S-fine Selmer group is trivial confirming the validity of Conjecture A", but Remark 1.4 states that Conjecture A "is true without the finiteness assumption of Ж^S(A/K_∞)" (citing [GJS22]). The claimed application is therefore not a new result and is presented misleadingly.
